title: Over-Synchronization in GPU Programs
problem: GPU programs fail to explicitly utilize advanced synchronization features like scopes, causing over-synchronization that wastes performance. Programmers unnecessarily perform global synchronization instead of scope-based synchronization within thread subsets.
motivation: Efficient synchronization across thousands of concurrent GPU threads is critical to GPU application performance.
method: ScopeAdvice analyzes CUDA programs to identify over-synchronization patterns by examining synchronization constructs. The tool characterizes three variants of over-synchronization by comparing actual synchronization scope requirements against what the program implements. It provides recommendations to replace global barrier calls with more efficient scope-based synchronization.
key_novelty: Systematic characterization of over-synchronization as a distinct performance anti-pattern in GPU programs with automated detection and diagnosis.
contributions: Demonstration that real-world GPU applications leave performance on the table through over-synchronization
Characterization of three variants of over-synchronization patterns observed in practice
ScopeAdvice tool for automated detection of over-synchronization in CUDA programs
Up to 55% performance improvement from fixing identified over-synchronization issues
